paper_metadata.title: Quantum Machine Learning methods for Fourier-based distribution estimation with application in option pricing

summary: The paper studies three gate-based quantum methods for European put option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics: two PQC-based Fourier-coefficient estimators and one QAMC/mRQAE benchmark. It reports 2-qubit circuits, 300 training epochs for the PQC methods, and about 5000 shots per coefficient on average for the QAMC benchmark, with convergence improving as dataset size and circuit size increase, but no practical quantum advantage is demonstrated.

experiments.description: Method I: supervised-learning PQC to approximate the underlying PDF and extract Fourier coefficients for European put option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics.

algorithm.variant: PQC-based supervised learning for PDF approximation
algorithm.ansatz: 2-qubit layered ansatz with Rx(x) data encoding and Ry(θ) trainable rotations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Input x is rescaled to [-π, π] and encoded via Rx(x) gates; trainable Ry(θ) layers follow each encoding block
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize empirical H1 risk for PDF approximation; then compute option price from Fourier coefficients of PDF and payoff
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Differential loss term using derivative information; no explicit hard constraints

problem_instance.description: European vanilla put option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics using a learned PDF of the normalized log-price variable

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes lognormal/normalized log-price distribution; strikes K=90,100,110; parameters S0=100, r=0.1, T=1, σ=0.25

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Logarithmic normalization by strike price; training on [-2π,2π] with data rescaled to [-π,π] to reduce Gibbs phenomena
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 repetitions; convergence assessed versus exact option price across dataset sizes and circuit sizes

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Rescale data to [-π, π]; compute Fourier coefficients of payoff analytically; DFT applied to trained circuit evaluations
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Convert complex Fourier coefficients ck to trigonometric coefficients Af_k and Bf_k; compute option price from coefficient products

results.unit: x6 minimum scheme; also 7x7 and 8x8 tested

experiments.description: Method III: gate-based QAMC benchmark using modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (mRQAE) to estimate Fourier coefficients of the PDF for option pricing.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Accelerated Monte Carlo with modified Real Quantum Amplitude Estimation (mRQAE)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: increasing tolerance in mRQAE; precision controlled by shots per coefficient

problem_formulation.encoding_details: State preparation encodes the asset-price distribution and payoff into amplitudes; Fourier coefficients estimated via amplitude estimation
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate Fourier coefficients Af_k and Bf_k of the PDF by sampling amplitudes corresponding to integrals of f(y|x) times sine/cosine basis functions
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: mRQAE used to recover sign of coefficients; no explicit penalty formulation

problem_instance.description: European vanilla put option pricing under Black-Scholes dynamics using QAMC as a benchmark for Fourier coefficient extraction

dataset_specification.description: Black-Scholes exact simulation; strikes K=90,100,110; parameters S0=100, r=0.1, T=1, σ=0.25

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Exact simulation of asset evolution assumed; coefficients estimated from discrete samples of the simulated distribution
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Convergence evaluated by varying shots/tolerance and comparing estimated prices across circuit sizes 6x6, 7x7, 8x8

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Analytical payoff coefficients C_k and D_k; exact simulation of Black-Scholes asset evolution assumed
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Combine estimated Fourier coefficients with payoff coefficients to compute option price
